changes: New character, status and episode-opening images use the exact gpt-image-2.5-flare model. Character portraits stay medium-quality 1K; approved sprites stay high-quality 2K with native PNG transparency.

Accepted versions, checkpoints and request receipts retain their model and approval semantics. Status sheets remain high-quality 1K transparent PNGs, and episode opening images remain high-quality 1K opaque PNGs.
Home invites you to create a character and dream with other creators in worlds with consistent rules. The group artwork meets the bottom-right banner edge and scales down on mobile.
Channel creators can rename a channel from Settings, with immediate heading updates and protection against stale edits. Staff and viewers cannot rename it.

The existing update_channel MCP tool now accepts name-only updates: omitted description and visibility are preserved. UI and MCP share validation and the database ownership/version lock; channel URLs, cast, episodes and publication stay unchanged.

The sign-in panel fills the height below the header with a thinner gray divider. Assistant guidance and the 79-tool contract are synchronized; explicit privacy changes and deletion keep their existing authorization requirements.
The website header shows Create only after sign-in. Theme controls are compact sidebar icons for all visitors, and account actions align consistently.

Channel headers use a clickable creator avatar beside the world badge. The existing get_public_profile tool provides the same published main character; episode titles omit the duplicate episode number.
Navigation guidance and the 79-tool contract are synchronized. Public profile reads, generation, publication and access rules are unchanged.
Theme controls live in the sidebar for every visitor. The signed-out header shows Create and Login; Connect your AI stays in the sidebar.

Mobile Search expands from an icon into a focused search field with close and Escape controls. Home shelves fit narrow screens, and personal channel cards have borders and stable loading/refresh behavior.
Website navigation guidance and the 79-tool contract are synchronized. Display preferences add no MCP operations; generation, publication and access rules are unchanged.
Create in the website header opens Connect your AI. My channels sits beside the world filters on the public and personal channel lists.
Channel cards use a responsive grid, the cloud keeps its original colors, and channel loading preserves the player and Studio selection while retaining account and access boundaries.
Navigation guidance and the exported 79-tool contract remain synchronized; generation, publication, subscriptions and deletion semantics are unchanged.

Home brings characters, channels and episodes together with compact world filters, a global Search and an expandable left sidebar. The existing ettu logo, character/version pages, creator Studio, settings and deep links remain accessible.

Channel subscriptions are private, distinct from character follows and grant no team access. Subscribe controls share desired-state validation with MCP; the subscription feed includes only public channels and published episodes with the selected ready video.

Six new tools cover grouped search, personal director/staff channels, subscription state, subscribe/unsubscribe, subscription lists and the chronological episode feed. Public browsing adds channels and all-world queries. Guidance and the 79-tool contract match the website.
Channel pages open on Watch, with a compact header and no director reports below playback. Studio presents Story, Video and Activity one at a time, with one selector for previous video versions.

Channel cards, Discover episodes and Featured in Channels reuse the reviewed opening frame already extracted from a published video, without another AI generation call. Thumbnails follow selected-video publication and withdrawal rules.

Existing MCP channel reads return latest_episode.preview_url, and video objects include thumbnail_url. Assistant guidance and the 73-tool contract match the simplified navigation; generation, approval and deletion rules are unchanged.

Character profiles show Featured in Channels with public episode previews, ordered by the most recent featured publication. The new list_character_channels read tool returns the same paginated list and links.
Featured appearances use the selected published video snapshot. Private channels, draft episodes, unselected renders and cast membership alone are excluded, including for connected owners.

My characters returns to navigation. The signed-in dropdown opens My settings, includes Connect your AI and offers a System/Light/Dark theme toggle. Guests retain Connect your AI in the main navigation. Assistant guidance and the public 73-tool contract match these changes.
Artwork options groups character downloads. Status controls use Draw again and Check request, with full owner-only errors under What happened? and the same durable generation requests.
Public character profiles group Appearance, Voice and extra traits under More about the character, with a Created by section at the bottom of the details column.
The loading face draws a white outline, black fill, eyes and mouth in sequence. Assistant guidance matches the simplified labels; MCP tools, approval and publication rules are unchanged.

Character versions put the picture and two choices first: I like it! approves that exact image and starts its animation; Try another look requests a new candidate. Approval and publication remain separate.

Make a new version and Try drawing again retain existing generation semantics. Character details, downloads, history and deletion are grouped into expandable sections with the same confirmation and ownership checks.

Character pages use less space above the tabs, a compact draft shortcut, and a shared sketching-face loading view to smooth initial loading. Reduced-motion preferences show a still logo. Assistant guidance and the public 72-tool contract match the new labels.

Initial character portraits and intentional redraws request medium-quality 1K images; approved 2K sprites and status loops remain high quality. Candidate request settings are frozen, exposed to owner reads and retained on delivery retries.
Transparent character artwork displays against yellow in the website, with Change status next to the current status. Original PNG files keep their alpha channel.

Episode planning and final video prompts allow dialogue, scene ambience and action sounds, with no background music, score or musical stingers. Fresh renders exclude clips made under the older audio policy.
get_live_status batches compact generation, image-approval and channel/episode progress with the same ownership, role and publication rules as full reads. Discover it before calling older servers.
Website status readers share one authenticated SSE connection, renew expiring sessions and fall back to a batched read during outages. Signed artwork URLs remain stable until renewal is needed.

Updated guidance and the public 72-tool contract explain current-state snapshots, bounded topics and retained command request keys. Status reads never generate, approve, retry, delete or publish anything.
New character versions use high-quality gpt-image-2 transparent PNGs: one 1K image for owner approval before a 2K eight-view sprite. PNG alpha and the exact approved portrait are preserved.

Website and MCP can retrieve, approve or redraw the exact candidate under the same version. get_character_image, confirm_character_image and regenerate_character_image share ownership, concurrency and durable request checks. Approval never publishes.

Creation and definition edits now require durable request_key values as well. Retry delivery with the original key and arguments. Failed sprites reuse approved images; failed quality-review originals remain inspectable after content review.
Completed and failed character attempts expose private original generated-image links separately from processed sprites in the website and authenticated MCP reads.

Whole-image content review is recorded before fitting, so originals survive layout and quality failures. New work retains every reviewed image attempt; older normalized checkpoints can expose their latest reviewed source.

Originals use the existing seven-day retention and short-lived signed links. Pending jobs keep the reviewed first-frame preview; content-rejected artwork remains unavailable. Reads never generate or publish artwork.
New character generations request one 2K eight-view sheet and preserve 768px frames in the sprite, portrait and rotating GIF. Existing artwork and saved 1K jobs keep their settings.
Creator pages and collections show the first content-reviewed frame while generation continues. Owner MCP reads offer the same private work-in-progress image through include_generated_frames.
Facing directions are more explicit for every angle and use the same definitions in generation, view classification and targeted repairs. Preview reads never generate or publish artwork.
Six new authenticated read tools provide public Discover search, character and creator profiles, published collections, recent followers, and existing artwork retrieval.
Request portraits or sprite sheets as inline MCP PNGs and original download links, or retrieve GIF and manifest links. Private versions remain owner-only and reads never start generation.

Whole-character deletion requires the exact current name and explicit confirmation in both the website and MCP, including deletion through the final private version. Ownership, references and concurrent changes are checked in the shared database boundary.
New character sprites use one eight-angle sheet and reuse those views for a rotating preview, removing the repeated idle frames. Historical layouts and idle GIF timing remain supported.

Body-height and ground-line guidance improves scale consistency across front, profile and back views. Gemini references keep their original dimensions to avoid compounded padding and apparent shrinkage.

Generation still targets #ffdf00, but quality review accepts close yellow shades and small background variations. Exact-color feedback no longer spends an image repair; substantial background defects and visible framing drift remain actionable.
Regenerate character retries a failed unpublished version under the same version number, with a fresh generation attempt and unchanged details. Ready artwork still creates a new private version.

MCP uses expected_revision_id to reject stale attempts. Durable receipts identify superseded failures without starting another job; previous attempts and retained reviewed frames remain inspectable through the website and get_character_version.

Generate new version in the character Versions tab refreshes ready artwork with unchanged details and current models. MCP regenerate_character now also accepts private, currently published and previously published ready sources.
The current published portrait anchors identity; each refresh creates a private version and leaves publication unchanged. Durable request recovery prevents duplicate generation after a lost response.
Restores the solid ettu face and lettering with matching public and packaged plugin icons.
Documents the signed-in account dropdown, My Profile shortcut from Discover, browser theme preference and separate Clerk sign-out and assistant connection revocation.

Character Settings groups Archive/Unarchive and confirmed deletion. Published and private characters can be deleted only without channel or episode references, including retained video snapshots. The new get_character_settings tool shares ownership and eligibility checks with the website.
My Profile opens on My characters and moves private account and assistant connection controls into Settings.

Episode reviews expose impact levels through website reports and MCP. Only significant rendering-style deviations trigger quality corrections; other quality findings remain advisory, and mandatory content checks remain separate. The existing one-correction limit is unchanged.

Opening-image failures preserve the actual provider reason instead of an incorrect interruption message. Character prompts explicitly request uniform solid sRGB #ffdf00 backgrounds; model-painted source pixels remain intact.
New character and status artwork uses fixed-camera, body-scale and resting-anchor guidance, with more of each source cell devoted to the complete character and props.

Accidental resting-position and camera-scale jumps produce anchor_drift quality feedback and use the existing bounded repair budget. Natural breathing, blinks and intentional status-action movement remain valid.

Existing published GIFs and delivery receipts remain intact. Improving existing artwork requires an explicitly requested new generation and separate publication approval; source resolution and GIF dimensions are unchanged.
Channel creators now find confirmed deletion under Settings → Danger zone on the channel details page. The same delete_channel MCP approval and ownership checks apply.
Channel deletion now supports Clerk accounts without a legacy Supabase login. Durable receipts preserve safe retries and report pending public-media removal.
The outlined et letters are slightly thicker across the website and downloadable wordmarks.

Channel creators can permanently delete a channel from the details page Danger zone, with typed-name confirmation. The delete_channel MCP tool requires explicit approval, the exact channel name and current version.

Deletion removes episodes, scenes, video history, memberships, invitations and proposals while preserving characters and existing inbox messages. Active videos must be stopped first. Durable receipts make identical retries safe and report pending public-media cleanup.
Thicker face outlines now match across the website, app icons, downloadable logo assets and plugin icons. Updated guidance and public 61-tool contract.

New character and status artwork retains Ettu yellow (#ffdf00) in both universes. Existing published files and exact restores keep their artwork; background changes do not authorize paid regeneration.
Updated plugin and skill icons use an outlined face with solid features on yellow, matching the website and downloadable brand assets.
The server uses linear sprite resampling to avoid introducing dark edge fringes. This does not remove lines already drawn in source images or change GIF color limits.
Refreshed assistant guidance and the public 60-tool contract. Server changes reach existing MCP connections; updating the plugin refreshes instructions and branding.

Failed character versions can be regenerated from the website version panel or the new regenerate_character MCP tool. A new private version copies the failed description and interview, preserves the failed attempt, and requires explicit publication.

Regeneration uses a durable UUID request_key. Reuse it after a timeout or lost response; a receipt survives version deletion and pruning. Active generation, ownership, archive and content-rejection checks apply equally in the UI and MCP.

New versions of published characters use the published portrait as an identity reference, preserving unchanged features while applying requested appearance changes. Current character and status sprites retain a full opaque white background.
Updated assistant guidance and the public 60-tool contract. MCP behavior updates on the server; updating this plugin refreshes its skill instructions.

Creator-only frame previews let users inspect retained, content-reviewed character sprites after a universe/style or other quality failure. get_character and get_character_version accept include_generated_frames=true; previewing never approves publication.

set_character_status can redraw even a completed status sprite/GIF with regenerate_animation=true and a UUID request_key. Reuse the key after an uncertain response. Pending generation is reused and the previous approved GIF remains visible through replacement generation or failure.
Creators can change a character’s status or request a redraw directly on its website profile. Status and artwork replacement remain separate from character versions.

Episode director planning and repair decisions now use GPT-5.6 Sol with medium reasoning; artwork reviews keep their separate model. Remote MCP updates server-side; updating this bundle refreshes assistant guidance.
The episode director now chooses the shortest suitable 4-, 6- or 8-second duration per shot. Auto timing is the default; seconds_per_scene is its ceiling. Explicit fixed timing remains available.

One targeted correction per started shot can remove an actual prohibited visual element, correct a disallowed line, or repair continuity. Ettu records the limitation, proposed fix, local/forward/full impact and final outcome, and rebuilds affected footage.

Studio and Channel show real director activity, corrective attempt numbers and immutable plan revisions. The read-only get_episode_video_report tool provides paged activity and optional historical plan/attempt evidence.

Unknown submissions, account/quota failures and unexplained likeness rejections are not automatically resubmitted. Correction work may incur additional usage; new paid renders still require user authorization. Remote MCP capabilities update server-side; update the plugin for this guidance.
Ettu now compiles narrative story scenes into as many or as few focused video shots as needed, preserving story order, cast and explicit dialogue. Users do not need to plan eight-second clips.
Studio and team MCP reads show the compiled video shot plan, original scene mapping, shot details, planned runtime and per-shot generation progress, including saved plans in video history.
The remote MCP update is automatic. Updating this bundle refreshes scene-writing guidance and explains that seconds_per_scene is now the duration per compiled shot.
Episode guidance now covers shared scene planning, reviewed opening frames, parallel rendering and exact continuations using the preceding final frame.

Requested retries can reuse compatible completed and reviewed clips; set reuse_completed_scenes=false for a fresh rendition. Updated MCP documentation explains per-scene Google/Ettu diagnostics and cancellation.
The rendering changes run on the Ettu server. Existing OAuth connections keep working; updating the plugin refreshes instructions and requires no provider API keys.

Updated the episode skill reference and MCP contract for server-selected image generation. New character images, status animations and episode opening frames use Gemini 3.1 Flash Image; artwork review remains separate.
This is a documentation update. Existing MCP connections receive the server-side image change without reinstalling; no provider API keys or endpoint changes are needed in the plugin.
Episode videos use Google Veo 3.1 with 720p, 16:9 widescreen output. Choose 4, 6 or 8 seconds per scene (default 8); OpenAI generates the opening frames.

Updated episode guidance and the public MCP contract cover supported durations, generation progress and explicit publication. Provider credentials remain on the Ettu server; the MCP connection and OAuth sign-in are unchanged.
Production ettu plugin for https://ettu.lol/mcp, with OAuth sign-in and installation guidance for Codex, Claude and ChatGPT.

Character interviews, permanent Clay and Anime universes, personality and voice direction, private artwork previews, version history and explicit publication. Names allow up to 100 characters; favorites and hates allow 3–50 distinct items each.
Live moods and activities with status GIFs generated on first use, plus public profiles, main characters, unique handles and following.

Story channels with director controls, cast invitations, episodes, scenes, staff proposals and private inbox conversations. Scene guidance preserves scenery, personality, voice and continuity; episode videos are published explicitly.
The ettu-update skill checks release metadata, explains available changes and guides the host’s plugin update process.
Yellow ettu dot branding for the plugin and both skills, with self-contained image assets and the public PNG at https://ettu.lol/brand/pwa-512.png.
Public MCP contract documentation includes all 55 tools, input schemas, permissions and workflow requirements.
